articles.title: Hegseth promises execution live stream as Trump appears to ‘pause’ war on Iran | First Thing
articles.summary: US president says US will not attack Iran before midterms, while defense secretary says Nidal Hasan will face a firing squad next month. Plus Sofia Coppola looks back on her glittering directorial…

blocks.text: Good morning. The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, has said the execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad will be livestreamed next month, in a radical departure from the previous norm. Hegseth said: “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand there’s serious consequences for these types of things.”

Hasan opened fire at a medical processing center at Fort Hood, Texas, on 5 November 2009, killing 13 people and wounding dozens more. A military jury sentenced him to death in 2013 and he has been held at Fort Leavenworth in Kansas ever since. The last known case of a military firing squad in the US was in November 1945.

items: Why is Hegseth being criticised over the Iran war? The Democratic senator Chris Murphy said Hegseth was “determined to hide the cost and the consequences of this war from the American public”. Murphy claimed the Pentagon blocked him from visiting a military base in Qatar and that an Iranian strike on the US embassy in Riyadh was far worse than the public were led to believe.

What has Donald Trump said about the US war on Iran? The US president has promised not to attack Iran before November’s US midterm elections, outlining a pause on the protracted war he has struggled to end after almost eight months. A Reuters/Ipsos survey from late September found that only about a third of Americans approved of the strikes on Iran.

articles.title: Leader of Jewish Greens calls for Zack Polanski to resign
articles.summary: Vivien Lichtenstein says party leader should stand down over ‘Zionism is racism’ policy after losing byelection

blocks.text: The leader of the Jewish Greens has called for Zack Polanski to step down as pressure increases on the Green leader to acknowledge anger within the party over a new policy which equates Zionism with racism and calls for the state of Israel to be abolished.

The comments by Vivien Lichtenstein come after Caroline Lucas, the Greens’ former leader and first MP, criticised Polanski for a lack of leadership in missing the debate and vote at the weekend which resulted in the policy being passed.

Lichtenstein had warned she was considering quitting the Green party of England and Wales in the wake of the vote at the party conference to adopt the policy, which states that Zionism is racism and calls for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state.
Polanski was not at the conference on Sunday when the motion was debated; instead he was campaigning for Holborn and St Pancras byelection, in which he finished second to Labour.

In post-byelection interviews, Polanski said he would have voted against the motion had he attended. Two amendments he supported, including one that called for a two-state solution rather than a single Palestinian state, were voted down.

Speaking to Times Radio, Lichtenstein said that even though Polanski was campaigning, he should have spoken and voted for the amendments online, which was an option. “He should have done that. And I think that was a big mistake on his part.”

Lichtenstein said she was surprised to hear Polanski say he had been working with Jewish members of the party, adding: “I don’t know which Jewish members of the party he’s been working with. It certainly hasn’t been with the Jewish Greens committee.”
Asked if he should continue in his role, she replied: “No, I think he should resign.”
Speaking to Newsnight on Thursday, before the byelection result, Lucas, who remains one of the Greens’ best-known and popular figures, said Polanski “should have been there and he should have voted”.

She went on: “I would have hoped that he would have really been a very strong critic of this motion, because the motion was flawed from top to bottom in my view. It’s dangerous, it’s divisive, it tries to have a singular definition of Zionism when we know that there are many.”
Asked if Polansksi should stand down, Lucas did not definitively say he should remain as leader: “I think let’s just see what happens in the… coming days and weeks.

“Obviously he has been completely taken up with this byelection. I want him to speak now about what’s happened. I want him to show the leadership that was frankly missing on Sunday. I think the jury is out about whether or not he will do that, but I very much hope he will. But that is a long way from full-throated support.”
Jonathan Bartley, who was formerly the Green co-leader with Lucas, and is now a councillor in Lambeth, south London, called on Polanski to “put his hands up” and apologise.
“I think [the policy vote] was a failure of leadership from Zack and there is a certain toxicity now from the Green party,” he told the BBC.

There is no formal mechanism for ejecting a leader of the Greens. However, they are re-elected every two years, meaning Polanski, who took over in September 2025, will have to go before party members again in less than a year.

articles.title: Former ICC judge Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
articles.summary: Navi Pillay is a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded that Israel committed genocide in Gaza

blocks.text: NOBEL PEACE PRIZE WINNER. An illustration of Peace Prize laureate Navanethem "Navi" Pillay after the announcement of the Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 at the Norwegian Nobel Institute, in Oslo, Norway October 9, 2026.
NTB/Javad Parsa/via REUTERS
Navi Pillay is a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded that Israel committed genocide in Gaza

OSLO, Sweden – Navi Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded that Israel committed genocide in Gaza, won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday, October 9, “for her efforts to promote peace and international law.”
This year’s Nobel Peace Prize underlined the importance of maintaining an organised international order, the committee said in its citation.
“The system of international law is under tremendous pressure, and its institutions are under attack,” it said.

“We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice. Whenever might overtakes right, it undermines stability, trust and peaceful co-existence.”

Born in Durban, in South Africa’s Natal province, in a family of Indian Tamil origin, Navi Pillay, 85, has been a judge on several international courts, including the International Criminal Court and the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda.

She was also chair of the UN Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory that concluded last year that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza. Israel dismissed the report as “scandalous”.
She has also served as United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.
In 1967 she became the first woman to start a law practice in Natal and the first non-white woman to serve on South Africa’s High Court.
Pillay held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict, and demonstrated a firm moral compass in her long career, said the committee.

“A common thread runs from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time,” said the citation.
The Hague-based ICC has been the target of an escalating campaign by US President Donald Trump, who last month urged countries to leave it.

Washington has already imposed targeted sanctions on several prosecutors and judges at the court and, according to sources, is considering wider sanctions in retaliation for the targeting of Israeli leaders.
The committee was not directly criticising Trump by rewarding Pillay, according to Haakon Gjerloew, acting director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo.

“I think it’s generally rather a promotion of an international legal world order. Of course, he might react to someone who has been part of the ICC, but it’s not a direct attack on Trump,” Gjerloew said.
The peace prize is the fifth Nobel awarded this week, after literature, chemistry, physics and medicine. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado won in 2025.

The Nobel Peace Prize, worth 12 million Swedish crowns, or about $1.2 million, is due to be presented in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the death of Swedish industrialist Alfred Nobel, who founded the awards in his 1895 will. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
articles.summary: The missile attacks come amid an escalation in fighting between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government.

blocks.text: Three Saudi nationals have been killed in two attacks on the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, the country's civil aviation authority has said after Yemen's Houthis said they targeted the facility.
The attacks also resulted in "injuries to a number of Saudi citizens and residents of various nationalities", the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement on X.
It said the first attack on Thursday targeted the airport while the second one struck an aircraft belonging to state carrier Saudia.
One of its pilots was among those killed, the airline said in a statement.
Air traffic had returned to normal, the civil aviation authority said.
Yemen's Houthi group said on Thursday it had attacked the airport with two missiles, reports said.
The Iran-aligned group said it had also targeted an airport in Najran city near the Saudi border with Yemen, and Khamis Mushait air base further north. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed these attacks.
The latest casualties follow the deaths of three people in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on October 6 and 7.
Two were killed and 28 wounded in an attack at Abha International Airport, the civil aviation body said on Wednesday. Another person was killed at King Khalid airport.
The latest attacks come amid mark an escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west.

The Houthi military spokesperson said the previous two attacks on Saudi Arabia's airports were in "response to the Saudi aggression against our country" which saw "60 airstrikes and missile attacks in the past 24 hours".
The group says it is targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war.
The conflict has worsened in recent weeks, after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.
That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping.
But Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.
A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government.

A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
But the informal ceasefire began to unravel in July.

The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating for what they say is a years-long Saudi blockade, and for an air strike on Sanaa airport.

articles.title: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season
articles.summary:
Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding

Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind…

blocks.text: Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

As a result of the strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.

Isaias is expected to make landfall on Friday evening local time, bringing an estimated 75-150mm (2.9-5.9in) of rainfall across the Gulf coast. There may be up to 250mm in places, with a possibility of flash flooding and isolated river flooding.

The NOAA also said there was increasing likelihood of life-threatening storm surge along portions of the northern Gulf coast and damaging hurricane-force winds over portions of the Florida panhandle, southern Alabama and Mississippi. A hurricane warning has been issued and people have been told to prepare for long power outages and to obey any evacuation orders issued.

blocks.caption: People pick up sandbags in Mobile, Alabama, in preparation for Hurricane Isaias. Photograph: Octavio Jones/AP

articles.title: 2 children dead after landslide hits uphill village in Cebu City
articles.summary: Residents in Barangay Pulangbato, Cebu City are being evacuated following the landslide

blocks.text: RESCUE. An individual was rescued during a search and retrieval operation following a landslide at Sitio Riverside in Barangay Pulangbato, Cebu City, on October 9, 2026.
Jacqueline Hernandez/Rappler
Residents in Barangay Pulangbato, Cebu City are being evacuated following the landslide
CEBU, Philippines – Two children died and one senior citizen remains missing after soil collapsed from an upland area in Barangay Pulangbato, Cebu City on Friday, October 9.

Pulangbato Barangay Councilor Kaven Seno told Rappler in an interview that heavy rains since the first week of October had softened the soil in the village’s upland area which later resulted in a landslide.
According to Cebu City Councilor Dave Tumulak, a family of four was buried in the debris due to the incident.

Tumulak said that a 5-year-old child was retrieved at around 1:45 pm but died while receiving emergency care at a hospital. At around 2:26 pm, a 38-year-old woman was extracted and is currently under hospital care.
At 4:24 pm, rescuers were able to extract a 6-year-old from the rubble but the child had already died.

Tumulak told reporters that the unstable terrain at the landslide site is making it difficult for search-and-rescue units to finish the extraction. As of this writing, a 60-year-old woman remains missing at the landslide site.

Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival, in an update at around 3:30 pm on Friday afternoon, said that rescue and retrieval operations are continuously underway and medical personnel are on the ground in Barangay Pulangbato.

Barangay officials have announced evacuations at the area due to safety concerns caused by the incident. Affected residents are currently being evacuated to the Pulangbato Gym. – with reports from Jacqueline Hernandez/Rappler.com

articles.title: Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream
articles.summary: Alonzo Lunsford tells the BBC the punishment befits the crime but he has some doubts whether the public should be able to watch it.

blocks.text: A former US Army sergeant who survived the mass shooting on Fort Hood has said that while he supports the execution of the gunman by firing squad, he is concerned about it being livestreamed.
Alonzo Lunsford, who was shot seven times, told the BBC that the "method is befitting" for Nidal Hasan because other methods like lethal injection would be "doing him a favour".
Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist, fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers in a medical building at Fort Hood in 2009.
But while Lunsford agreed with the method, he said the execution is "not something you should view for entertainment purposes".

Speaking to Radio 4's Today programme on Friday, he said: "To show the whole thing without it being censored for the general public, for me personally, I don't agree with that, but it's not about my personal belief."
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the public will be able to view a livestream of the execution, saying it is important for people to see the consequences of this kind of crime.
If it goes ahead, and legal experts told the BBC it might not ever happen, it would be the first public execution in the US in almost a century.

Lunsford explained that while he is concerned about the "effect" and "message" a livestream would send to younger people, when it comes to the survivors, their families and the families of the victims, they "should be able to look at it".

"I'm gonna be there [to watch in person] and before they pull the trigger, I want him to look at me in my eyes and I look at him in his eyes and I want him to know: 'Dude you failed, I'm still here,'" he said.

"I don't really have any sympathy for him as far as firing squad vs lethal injection, hanging or gas chamber, because he didn't have that same compassion when he did the deed on 5 November," the former sergeant explained.
"I think the method is befitting for him because the lethal injection - that's doing him a favour. Gas chamber? Is doing him a favour."
But Lunsford said that as a Christian, he has forgiven Hasan because "I cannot heal if I don't forgive him".
"We're taught that with your last breath you can ask for forgiveness and I think that's what he [Hasan] should do," he added.
Telling his account of what happened that day, he said Hasan got out of his chair and jumped onto a counter, before pulling out a weapon and discharging rounds.

Lunford said he was looking for an exit via the back door, which was "two or three strides" away from him when he was first shot above his left eye and then "hit two more times in my back" as he crawled behind a desk.
"At that point I played dead," he said. When Hasan moved on, he grabbed a nearby wounded soldier and went outside, where Lunsford said Hasan came up behind them and shot him again.
One memory he said that "bothers" him from the day was of a woman who told Hasan she was pregnant.
"We heard a gunshot and the last thing that girl was saying was: 'Oh my god, my baby, my baby.'"
Lunsford said personnel don't carry weapons in medical facilities, and that Hasan "took the coward's way out" to attack them there.
"And then for him to say he is fighting for his cause? I've read the Quran, and everything that he said he was doing that was in the Quran is not supported by the Quran," he explained.
Hasan's execution was announced by the Pentagon earlier this week, in what will be the first military execution in more than 60 years.
Legal experts have told the BBC there are a number of hurdles around the livestreaming of this which could mean it is successfully challenged in court.
Some politicians have been vocal in their opposition.
Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN it was "disgusting" while Republican Senator Thom Tillis said public executions were what "oppressive dictators" did.
"It should not be happening in America," he added in a post on X., external

articles.title: Palace hopes Duterte stays healthy to ‘admit’ drug war killings at ICC
articles.summary: Malacañang welcomed the ruling saying it is also their hope that Duterte will remain healthy amid the proceedings.

blocks.text: Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang said it is hoping that former President Rodrigo Duterte will remain in good health at the International Criminal Court (ICC) so he can personally attend his trial and “admit” to the drug war killings.
Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said at a press briefing in Singapore on Friday, October 9, that Duterte can only face the allegations against him if he remains in good condition.

“Dahil sa kanyang malusog na pangangatawan, malusog na pag-iisip, doon lamang niya maaaring isiwalat ang katotohanan,” Castro said. “At malamang ay mabanggit niya rin sa hearing kapag panahon na niyang magsalita ang pag-amin niya sa mga isinagawang planong pagpapatay para sa paglaban umano sa droga.”

(Because only if he remains physically and mentally well can he reveal the truths. And perhaps, he can mention during the hearing, once it is his turn to testify, his admission of the planned killings for his war on drugs.)

The comment came after the ICC earlier ruled that Duterte is fit to stand trial and capable of understanding the proceedings in his crimes against humanity case for murder, despite previous concerns about his health.
The ruling, according to the ICC’s decision released publicly on October 8, was based on reports from three medical experts who examined Duterte’s condition.
It found that Duterte is capable of not only understanding the proceedings and the charges against him but also instructing his counsel in preparing his defense.
The ICC said it found no evidence to support the Duterte camp’s previous claim that the former president is suffering from “significant memory impairment.”
Malacañang welcomed the ruling, saying it also hopes that Duterte will remain healthy amid the proceedings.

“‘Yun naman din po ang nais natin,” Castro said. “Unang-una, ang nais lahat ng mga Pilipino ay maging maayos ang kalusugan ng dating Pangulong Duterte, mas maging malakas siya, mas maging malalim ang kanyang pag-iisip para maharap niya ang mga akusasyon na ibinabato sa kanya.”
(That’s also what we want. First of all, all Filipinos want Duterte to be healthy, stronger, and to have better mental well-being so he can face the accusations thrown against him.)

articles.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law
articles.summary: Norwegian committee recognises achievements of former UN rights chief who stood up against apartheid in South Africa
articles.byline: Guardian staff and agencies in Oslo

blocks.text: Former UN human rights chief Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a judge on the international court of justice (ICJ), has won the Nobel peace prize.

Pillay, 85, from South Africa, who is a judge with the international court of justice, was recognised for her efforts to promote peace and international law, said Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel committee.

“A common thread runs from her early work ⁠defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood ​up against ‌apartheid to ‌her service as a judge in some ‌of the key international court cases of our time,” the committee said.

“At a time when the number of wars and conflicts is rising, and when judges and institutions of international law are under political attack, the Nobel committee wishes to issue a reminder that the ability to resolve conflicts without force or violence is dependent on the international rule of law.
“An international legal system in which war criminals are held to account and the victims of abuse see justice served is a precondition for a peaceful world.”
Pillay headed the UN independent international commission of inquiry, which does not speak on behalf of the world body and that last year found genocide was occurring in Gaza.
Pillay told Agence France-Presse at the time that her team had shared “thousands of pieces of information” with prosecutors at the international criminal court.
The UN said the awarding of the Nobel peace prize to Pillay highlighted the importance of international human rights.

“It’s wonderful to see this being awarded to Navi Pillay, the former high commissioner for human rights. It is testament to the need and to the value of human rights in this world more than ever,” said Shabia Mantoo, spokesperson for the UN human rights agency.

The committee, based in Oslo, received nominations for 287 candidates for this year’s prize, and just over a quarter of those were for organisations. Experts say the committee typically focuses on the durability of peace, the promotion of international fraternity and the quiet work of institutions that strengthen those goals.

Last year, the Venezuelan opposition leader, María Corina Machado, won the Nobel peace prize for her struggle to achieve a democratic transition in the South American nation, winning recognition as a woman “who keeps the flame of democracy burning amid a growing darkness”.

Machado gave her Nobel medal to Donald Trump shortly after the United States ousted the then Venezuelan president, Nicolás Maduro. But it was largely a symbolic gesture: the Nobel committee has said the honour itself cannot be transferred.

Nominations can be made by a select group of people and organisations, including heads of state or politicians serving at a national level, university professors, directors of foreign policy institutes, past Nobel prize recipients and members of the Norwegian Nobel committee itself.

Four of this year’s Nobels were announced earlier this week. The Nobel for medicine went to three scientists whose work led to a tool that uses light to help unravel how the brain works. The physics award recognised a scientist’s efforts to demystify a rare group of neutrinos. The chemistry prize recognised two scientists for untangling mysterious mirror images in molecules, a discovery that has been used to develop countless drugs.
More details soon …

articles.title: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for 'prioritising safety'
articles.summary: The AI firm instead claims the researchers were fired for mishandling sensitive information.

blocks.text: Three former OpenAI researchers sacked for allegedly mishandling information claim they were instead let go because they raised safety concerns at the tech firm.

"I believe we were fired for prioritising safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation," Mikita Balesni posted on X, external alongside an open letter to the ChatGPT-maker, written with fellow ex-employees.
On 2 October, a spokesperson for the AI firm told the BBC its investigation "confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures".
OpenAI repeated these claims, external on Friday morning in a note from research leaders.
"We want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out," the note said.
"Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what's outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment."
The dismissals come amid a growing debate over AI safety and the potential risks advanced AI systems could pose to society.
The joint letter to OpenAI leadership was written by Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, who say they were all, until recently, safety or alignment employees at the company.
Alignment is the practice of building human ethical ideas and principles into the technology. In other words, it aims to keep it on track with what humans value.

The former staff members raised concerns that their firings had made employees at the tech company "afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI".

Reposting the letter, Korbak wrote, external: "For months, I'd been raising safety concerns that we're losing the ability to monitor what AI agents think, one of our best tools for catching when they misbehave.
"I believe that was why I was fired."
OpenAI said it was finalising contracts with third-party safety assessors and would announce details in the coming weeks.
"We were not the first to be pushed out of OpenAI under suspicious circumstances," Wang said in a post on X, external.
"Unless the employees take a stand now against this kind of manoeuvre, I am concerned we will not be the last."

articles.title: South Africa pulls asylum directive after violent protests
articles.summary: South Africa has withdrawn a controversial asylum directive that sparked widespread protests in the country.

image.caption: Many protested against the new directive that would allow some migrants who had arrived in the country illegally to apply for asylumImage: Oupa Nkosi/REUTERS

blocks.text: South Africa has halted a new directive for the processing of asylum applications after violent protests broke out in Johannesburg and Durban.
The directive was issued by the Department of Home Affairs in response to a court judgement.
The court ruling said asylum seekers could not be denied access to South Africa's asylum system solely on procedural grounds, such as entering the country illegally.
That decision led to days of protests in the major coastal city of Durban, which then spread to Johannesburg's Soweto township on Thursday.
Rioters torched 14 cars in Durban and 10 in Soweto. Shops were looted in both locations.
What do we know about protests in South Africa?
The unrest in Durban followed a protest by a group demanding that a refugee center stop processing asylum applications. Vehicles were overturned and set on fire. Foreign-owned shops were also looted.
Meanwhile, in Soweto, residents clashed with foreign shop owners, and gunshots were heard, according to the broadcaster Newzroom Afrika.
Several vehicles were set alight during clashes, said Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department spokesman Superintendent Xolani Fihla in an interview with SABC television.
"It's reported that there were clashes between foreign nationals in the area and South African nationals," he said. "At the present moment, I can confirm that no injuries have been reported."

blocks.caption: Police fired rubber bullets when clashes erupted between protesters and foreign nationals in DurbanImage: Rajesh Jantilal/AFP

blocks.text: What is the court ruling that sparked protests?
The court ruling that sparked the flare-up of xenophobic tensions deemed certain provisions of the government's refugee policy to be unconstitutional.
The court said that this was because the provisions prevented individuals from accessing the asylum system on procedural grounds, such as entering the country illegally.
Recently, this ruling has led hundreds of people, reportedly including those who do not qualify for asylum, to flock to government refugee centers.
On Wednesday, the government emphasized that the judgement "does not grant refugee status or permanent residence automatically to anyone who enters South Africa."
Immigrants in South Africa pushed out of their own shops
Xenophobic sentiment in South Africa: What to know
South Africa has experienced months of anti-immigrant protests this year. Populist and anti-immigrant groups have demanded that undocumented foreign nationals leave by June 30.
Amidst international criticism, tens of thousands of people have fled the country, while some were repatriated by their governments.
Although South Africa has a third of its population unemployed, it remains the largest economy in Africa and continues to attract migrants.
Migrants are often blamed for taking jobs, fueling crime, and straining public services. However, social scientists have said these accusations are not supported by evidence.

articles.title: Germany women's football team: Can Ena Mahmutovic make a case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper?
articles.summary: The women's friendlies against Australia and Japan present an opportunity for Ena Mahmutovic to make her case for succeeding Ann-Katrin Berger as Germany's first-choice goalkeeper.

image.caption: Ena Mahmutovic is seen as the most likely candidate to become Germany's first-choice goalkeeper in futureImage: Martin Agüera/kolbert-press/picture alliance

blocks.text: Having qualified for next summer's World Cup in Brazil, the German women's national team is wrapping up this year's schedule with friendlies against Australia this Friday and Japan next Tuesday, and the choice of opponents was deliberate.
"Their style of play isn't what we're used to in Europe. That's what I want to prepare my team for," Germany coach Christian Wück said.
"These will be high-level matches, and they will challenge us in a completely different way than European teams do."
Wück said that his team had built a "solid foundation" over the past few years and that now it was all about taking the "next step" in their development.
"We are looking to continue along this path and refine it," he said.
"We know our strengths, but we need to utilize them 100% against top teams if we are going to hold our own," sporting director Nia Künzer said.
Can Mahmutovic seize her chance in goal?

Much like it was with the men's team during Jürgen Klopp's first international break as Germany head coach, the question as to who will emerge as the next number one goalkeeper for the women is also a hot topic.

blocks.caption: The understudy and the current No.1: Ena Mahmutovic and Ann-Katrin BergerImage: Madeleine Fantini/HMB Media/picture alliance

blocks.text: The difference is that unlike Manuel Neuer, who has retired from international football, Ann-Katrin Berger is sticking around for at least one more tournament cycle.
However, with just three matches to go before the start of the playoffs in the National Women's Soccer League, where she plays for Gotham FC, Berger is giving these two Germany friendlies a miss.
Parallels to men's goalkeeping situation
This means 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper Ena Mahmutovic, who is seen as a potential successor to Berger, is set to get her chance to shine.
"Ena deserves to play the next match," Wück told the prematch press conference in Karlsruhe on Thursday.
"We must not forget that she already kept a clean sheet in Slovenia (Germany's last World Cup qualifier). And I hope she can repeat that tomorrow."

Some will draw parallels to Jonas Urbig, who many see as a future number one for Germany's men. Both he and Mahmutovic were born in 2003 in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia, and both are seen as up-and-coming stars for their club and country.

blocks.caption: Manuel Neuer remains the first choice at Bayern, while Jonas  Urbig looks set to become Germany's No. 1Image: Frank Hoermann/SvenSimon/picture alliance

blocks.text: The difference is that while Urbig remains an understudy to Neuer at Bayern, Mahmutovic is already the first-choice keeper at her club, having won the starting job over Maria Luisa Grohs prior to the start of the season.
For Germany, though, Mahmutovic still has to bide her time, while there are already strong indications that Klopp intends to make Urbig his number one.
'The future of the national team'
"I'm obviously delighted," Mahmutovic said with a view to the upcoming friendlies.
"It's always something special, of course – especially playing against a team from another continent. I think testing ourselves against them is very helpful as we look ahead to the World Cup."
Bayern director Bianca Rech recently described Mahmutovic as "the future of the national team," calling on Wück not only to give her a callup, but also regular playing time.
Wück still sees Berger as slightly better than Mahmutovic, but he is also full of praise for the young keeper.
"Ena's performances have been very good," he said. "She will get her playing time."

blocks.caption: When Ena Mahmutovic lost control of the ball after a backpass, Italy's Sofia Cantore took full advantageImage: David Inderlied/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Costly mistake in Germany debut

The match against Slovenia was just Mahmutovic's second appearances for Germany. Her first, which came almost two years ago, was memorable for the wrong reason. In the dying minutes of a friendly in December 2024, she lost control of the ball after a back pass, allowing an Italian forward to score the winner in a 2-1 defeat for Germany. Still, Mahmutovic was included in Germany's squad for the 2025 Euros.
Had it been up to her father – who is from Montenegro – Mahmutovic would never have become a goalkeeper.
"He still says I would have been better as an outfield player because I'm good with both feet," she said.
Unusual Bundesliga debut

That's a quality that evidently wasn't lost on Thomas Gerstner, when her coach at her then-club Duisburg, gave her her Women's Bundesliga debut in May 2020. With the team coping with several absences, the then-16-year-old, who had been on the bench as backup goalkeeper, came on as an outfield player.
"The coach brought me on during stoppage time," Mahmutovic recalled. "I got to make two sprints – that was my debut."
That, however, was a one-off, and nobody questions Mahmutovic's strengths as a goalkeeper.
"She is one of the most talented goalkeepers in the world," said Bayern coach Jose Barcala, noting that she is the kind of player who can decide a match.
Mahmutovic will be hoping she gets many more opportunities to do just that for Germany.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Villanueva flags Cale88's P150 million sales with only 2 staff in 2024
articles.summary: Senator-judge Joel Villanueva on Friday questioned how Cale88 Foods Corporation generated P150 million in sales in 2024 despite having only two employees at the time.

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 5:17pm
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva on Friday questioned how Cale88 Foods Corporation generated P150 million in sales in 2024 despite having only two employees at the time.

On Day 37 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Villanueva raised a question about the food company listed as the business interest of Mans Carpio, the vice president’s husband. Villanueva asked the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Office of the Commissioner chief of staff Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez, about the firm’s sales and losses in 2024.
“Based po dito, may sales po sila na P150,595,605 na exempt at may sales din po na under sa—subject to regular income tax na P169,564 or a total of P150,765,259,” Garcia-Marquez said.
Garcia-Marquez also said that the company had expenses amounting to P11,428,809.
Villanueva, referring to the company’s general information sheet, questioned how the company could have P150 million in sales but only have two employees.

“Kasi gusto kong malaman bakit ganun? Dalawa lang yung employees na submitted? Around P150 million ang reported sales and based on previous witnesses, nabanggit pa yung foreign transactions. Senator Risa made mention of this. Kung kaunti lang yung employees, paano po yun? Paano na-handle yung, uh, ganitong kalaking operations?,” Villanueva said.

(I want to know why? There are just two employees submitted? And P150 million in reported sales, and based on the previous witness, foreign transactions were mentioned. Senator Risa made mention about this. If there were only a few employees, how is that? How was it handled for this huge operation?)
The BIR witness said that she could not say for certain as she was not with that company, but maintained that it was hard to reconcile.
“If ganito po at manufacturer po siya ng… banana chips, then parang impossible po unless naka-machine sila ng dalawang employee lang,” Garcia-Marquez said.
(If they are a manufacturer of banana chips, then it seems impossible unless they have a machine just for two people.)

Villanueva also tried to ask Garcia-Marquez about the list of wages of Cale88’s employees in 2023, but the latter remarked that she does not have those details. However, he noted that there were P23 million in gross sales in 2023, according to the company’s general information sheet. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Thieves steal 30,000 wine bottles worth €5m in Italy, reports say
articles.summary: The heist at the Florence-based winery is believed to be one of the largest thefts of its kind in Italy.

blocks.text: Thieves have stolen 30,000 bottles of wine collectively worth about €5m (£4.2m) from a prestigious Italian winery, Italian media reports.

Marchesi Antinori, one of Italy's biggest family-owned wineries, said the theft at its storage facility in Tuscany took place on Saturday as the company was preparing to ship a consignment to customers abroad.

At least seven masked men are believed to have deactivated the alarms, disabled the cameras and used company forklifts to load two large trucks of the company's prized Tignanello, Solaia and Guado al Tasso Tuscan reds.
Renzo Cotarella, the chief executive, told Corriere della Sera this was the largest theft of its kind in Italy.
"A theft of this scale and value has certainly never occurred in Italy," he said.
He added that he was hopeful the authorities would be able to trace the stolen wine.

"Two trucks full of merchandise can't just disappear into thin air. The Tuscan roads are full of cameras; perhaps with a bit of luck we'll be able to recover at least some of the bottles stolen from us."
He told the Financial Times: "These wines have a great value and I don't know how they can sell all this wine around the world without being seen."
The company believes the selection of bottles, which usually sell for between €150 and €500 each, suggests the thieves were wine connoisseurs and had inside knowledge.
The theft was only discovered on Monday morning as staff arrived on site. No arrests have been made.
Marchesi Antinori was founded in 1385 and exports to 170 countries. It had a revenue of €263m (£223m) last year.
There has been a spate of wine thefts in Italy this year, including two in the northern Piedmont region where hundreds of thousands of euros worth of bottles were reportedly taken.

articles.title: Who is Alexander Cabrera, the financial forensic analyst witness?
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel on Friday presented Alexander Cabrera, the financial forensic analyst who is expected to tie together the tax and financial records of Vice President Sara Duterte and her…

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 5:08pm

The House prosecution panel on Friday presented Alexander Cabrera, the financial forensic analyst who is expected to tie together the tax and financial records of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.

Cabrera faced the court on the 37th Day of Duterte’s impeachment trial. Before he was presented however, Defense counsel Sheila Sison raised an issue with the witness, questioning why Cabrera was allowed access to confidential documents.
House prosecutor Rep. Chel Diokno argued that the documents were already declared to be public, adding that it was standard practice for lawyers to consult experts for their cases.

Impeachment presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero also said that it was standard for experts to be given legally-acquired materials for their insights, saying that the defense was free to raise questions during their cross-examination.
Diokno then proceeded to establish Cabrera’s credibility as an expert.

Cabrera said that he graduated high school from Our Lady of Peace in Antipolo, Rizal. He then acquired his degree in Bachelor of Science in Business Administration and Accountancy from the Philippine School of Business Administration.

He went on to become a certified public accountant in 1988 and began work as a staff auditor at the accounting firm, Isla Lipana & Co, which is internationally known as the PwC Philippines. The firm is a member of the PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) network.

Since then, he rose through the ranks to become a senior associate in the tax department, and then became a senior manager before becoming a managing partner. He eventually became the vice chair of the firm before assuming the post of chair.
He retired from the firm in 2025 as the Chair Emeritus.
Part of his work was detecting fraud in financial records, saying that in his nearly 40 years, he has analyzed thousands of mergers and acquisitions.

Forensic audit was part of Cabrera’s job, saying that he had also spent thousands of hours on cases. During Diokno’s questioning, Cabrera said that he considered tax structuring and tax planning as his specialties.

Cabrera has also served as a resource person for legislative hearings in multiple hearings in Congress, saying that he offered his expertise in taxation. He has also worked in Congressional technical working groups. He estimated that he offered his expertise to Congress almost 100 times.
He also has a column in The Philippine Star called the “As easy as ABC”, where he talks about business and other national matters. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: BIR witness confirms issuance of LOA to Mans Carpio's CALE88
articles.summary: The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) has issued a letter of authority (LOA) for Cale88 Foods Corporation, one of the listed business interests of lawyer Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 5:07pm

The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) has issued a letter of authority (LOA) for Cale88 Foods Corporation, one of the listed business interests of lawyer Manases Carpio, husband of Vice President Sara Duterte.

This was confirmed by BIR Office of the Commissioner chief of staff Atty. Anne Loraine Garcia-Marquez on the 37th day of the impeachment trial, where the Vice President’s alleged unexplained wealth was being scrutinized.

During his interjection, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian pointed out the discrepancy between the declared sales of CALE88 to BIR amounting to P208 million, and its remittances worth P700 million as found by the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC).
The witness explained that inflows may be loans or any kind of donations, but emphasized that the company should still declare such funds in the financial statements.

“This should have been declared in the audited financial statement dahil…nandito lahat ng cash flow statement wherein dapat lahat ng galaw ng cash ng isang company ay nakalagay. So any inflow na na-receive ng company should've been declared in the audited financial statement,” Garcia-Marquez explained.

(This should have been declared in the audited financial statements because… the cash flow statement is in here, reflecting all of the company’s cash movements. So, any inflow received by the company should have been declared in the audited financial statement.)
“As to those na outside or hindi na-declare sa audited financial statement, maraming pong possibilities but hindi ko masasabi, Your Honor,” she added.
(As for those that are outside or not declared in the audited financial statements, there are many possibilities, which I cannot say for sure, Your Honor.)
Gatchalian then asked Garcia-Marquez if such a scenario would make CALE88 a candidate for the issuance of a LOA from the BIR.
“In fact, Your Honor, meron na pong letter of authority,” the witness answered.
Gatchalian clarified, “Ah, so meron na nga siyang letter of authority, so iniimbestigahan na itong company na ito?”
(So it already has a letter of authority, meaning this company is already being investigated?)
The BIR official answered in the affirmative.
The Senate President asked about possible penalties if a company is found not declaring sales.

“Under declaration po ng sales, magko-compute po tayo dito ng deficiency taxes. Meron po kasing civil and merong criminal cases. So sa civil, dito pumapasok ‘yung mga deficiency taxes na dapat bayaran. At kapag napatunayan na may tax evasion man, then dito papasok ang sa criminal case,” Garcia-Marquez said.

(Regarding the declaration of sales, we will compute the deficiency taxes here. We have civil and criminal cases. Civil cases cover the deficiency taxes that must be paid, while criminal cases come into play if tax evasion is proven.)
During Thursday’s trial, the BIR official said the agency found no records of the transfer of shares of stock of Cale88 to Pikimong Pikimong Corporation.

Cale88 is one of the business interests listed under the joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) of Duterte and her husband in multiple years, including the years when the Vice President already assumed office. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias ‘biggest test’ for Fema since Trump cuts, experts warn
articles.summary:
Gulf officials say they are ready for storm but concerns raised about restructured agency’s ability to respond effectively

Gulf state officials say they are prepared for Hurricane Isaias,…

blocks.text: Gulf state officials say they are prepared for Hurricane Isaias, but the storm could be the first major test of Fema’s ability to deploy a large surge workforce after the Trump administration’s sweeping cuts and restructuring of the agency, emergency management experts say.

The Trump administration has said it wants to eliminate, or drastically downsize, Fema, putting more burden on states. More than 4,300 employees left the agency in fiscal year 2025, about 17% of the workforce, according to a recent US government accountability office (GAO) report. The agency’s staffing reductions were not carried out systematically to ensure Fema could still meet its statutory obligations, said Chris Currie, director of homeland security and justice at the GAO.
“It’s not whether Fema is going to respond. They’re going to respond. It’s more about the depth,” Currie said.

One of the ways that staff was reduced at the agency was through early retirement, meaning many of those who left were more experienced people. From January 2025 to January 2026, 58 senior executive service employees left Fema, according to the GAO report. In the prior three fiscal years, the agency reported about 13 senior executive service separations on average per year.

Among the top officials who left the agency last year was the region four administrator, who oversees eight states, including Florida and Alabama, where Hurricane Isaias is expected to make landfall late Friday or early Saturday. Deanne Criswell, who led Fema under the Biden administration, said it was less about the number of people who left the agency and more about the loss of experience. “My biggest concerns are always the loss of institutional knowledge. You lose that knowledge. You lose the people who had been through these big disasters in the past,” she said.
In a written statement, Fema said the agency is actively monitoring and preparing for Hurricane Isaias.

“Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin’s leadership, the safety of the American people is DHS’s top priority,” the agency said. “Fema incident management assistance teams are deploying to Alabama and Florida, and Fema personnel are embedded in state emergency operations centers. Fema is also prepositioning emergency supplies at Maxwell air force base in Montgomery, Alabama, to supplement state resources if requested.”

Governors of Florida, Georgia and Alabama have declared states of emergency for counties projected to be affected by Hurricane Isaias. State emergency management personnel in Louisiana and Mississippi said they have been in regular contact with Fema and received full support from the agency earlier this year during Tropical Storm Arthur, which brought flash flooding and tornadoes across the Gulf coast.

At a news conference on Thursday, Jared Perdue, the Florida division of emergency management executive director, said the state has had very close coordination with their federal partners at Fema. But Currie warned that the agency could quickly find itself stretched thin if it has to respond to more than one natural disaster, a possibility that could become quickly consequential as El Niño strengthens and the agency heads into the fall and winter months.

blocks.caption: People prepare for the arrival of Hurricane Isaias in Pensacola, Florida. Photograph: Joe Raedle/Getty Images

blocks.text: “The bigger risk is how big it is and a second disaster happening and their ability to staff those,” he said. For example, In 2024, Hurricanes Helene and Milton made landfall in Florida less than two weeks apart. In response, Fema deployed 13,500 employees, straining staff capacity. “Fema has struggled to have the right number of people with the right qualifications, even before these cuts,” Currie said.

In June, Fema had active recovery efforts for over 1,000 open emergency disaster declarations. If the agency is forced to deploy personnel to multiple new disasters, as it did in 2024, Fema would likely have to marshal staff from these other active recovery efforts, putting those efforts on hold, Currie said. “Even though it’s been said that it’s been a quiet hurricane season, it could still be a busy disaster season,” he said.

Last month, a federal judge ruled that the Trump administration’s plan to cut Fema staff by 50% was unlawful. The administration has been slow to approve major disaster funding this year, according to an analysis by the Texas Tribune. Most major disaster declarations by Fema in 2026 came a month after the initial request, about three times longer than average, according to the report.

Ginny Goldman, the founder of Rebuild: the National Disaster Survivors Association, a member organization of climate disaster survivors, said those who went through the flooding in Texas Hill Country this summer still have not received FEMA individual assistance. In a Truth Social post, Donald Trump said the federal government would send $50m for disaster recovery assistance.

blocks.caption: People in Mobile, Alabama, pick up sandbags in anticipation of the storm. Photograph: Octavio Jones/AP

blocks.text: “Where is it at? What about the folks struggling to get back on their feet?” Goldman asked. Hurricane Isaias would be the “biggest test of Fema” since the Trump administration’s staffing cuts, she said. “And it’s coming at a challenging time because there are so many other compounding factors that are making life hard for people in America.”

While Gulf state officials have not expressed concern that Fema’s staffing cuts could impact the agency’s ability to respond to Hurricane Isaias, Goldman said disaster survivors are likely to notice. “If you’re a disaster survivor that is trying to navigate a system that is already broken, versus a civil servant in a government agency that is used to navigating a broken system day-to-day, you will have a different perspective on whether it’s broken or not,” she said.

articles.title: Labour chair of housing committee calls for urgent funds for affordable homes in England
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Abena Oppong-Asare urges chancellor to unlock billions of pounds, as housing associations say they could build 41,000 homes in 10 years

The Labour chair of the Commons housing…

blocks.text: The Labour chair of the Commons housing committee is urging John Healey to bring forward billions of pounds of planned spending on social and affordable homes in England, after housing associations said they were ready to build tens of thousands more.
Abena Oppong-Asare called for the chancellor to allocate money from the £39bn Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) as soon as possible, rather than after the election as planned.
Housing associations have said they could build an additional 41,000 homes outside London over the next 10 years if they had more government funding.

They said the extra units would help the government get closer to its target of building 1.5m new homes across this parliament – though the housing secretary, Angela Rayner, recently admitted that it would be difficult to achieve.

Oppong-Asare said: “The government should use the upcoming budget to increase the building of social homes by ensuring a significant proportion of the Social and Affordable Homes Programme is allocated during this parliament.

“Families stuck on social housing waiting lists need to see action now. I urge the chancellor to ensure a significant sum of the £39bn SAHP is allocated during this parliament and that truly affordable social rent homes are prioritised as part of this package.”
Healey’s predecessor, Rachel Reeves, announced the £39bn 10-year fund last year, having changed the government’s borrowing rules to allow her to borrow more for capital projects.
The money was due to be spent on a mix of council houses and a number of other types of affordable housing, including affordable rents and shared ownership schemes.
Before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had said the scheme should be reallocated entirely to social rent housing.
But when the first £10bn was allocated under his government in August, it went to a mix of councils and housing associations outside London to spend on a variety of types of subsidised homes.

Ministers said the money would help build 70,000 new homes. But housing associations said they could have built an additional 41,000 – including 25,000 for social rent – if the government had given them all the money for which they bid.
They said they could start construction work on 15,000 of those in the next three years – though some associations have come under fire for selling their homes to the private sector.
The National Housing Federation (NHF), which represents housing associations, said ministers would have to allocate an additional £5.3bn from the programme to build the extra homes.

Ministers have said they are planning to allocate £6bn to London immediately. But of the remaining £13bn, they said they planned to hand out “significant sums” in the second half of the scheme, which would come after the next election.

Kate Henderson, the chief executive of the NHF, said: “Housing associations submitted bids with plans to build tens of thousands of affordable homes, but many organisations with sites ready to go and proven track records did not receive the funding needed to deliver these homes.
“With additional investment now, it is possible to help transform the lives of families in urgent need of an affordable home.”

A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing said: “We’ve already announced nearly £10bn of allocations from the Social and Affordable Homes Programme so we can start building more than 70,000 council, social and affordable homes across England.
“Our record investment will help families trapped in temporary accommodation or stuck on housing waiting lists into safe, secure homes.”

articles.title: Palace: Duterte's good health to allow him to stand trial, reveal truth on drug war killings
articles.summary: Malacañang welcomed the ruling declaring former president Rodrigo Duterte fit to stand trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC), stating that Filipinos hope he remains healthy enough to…

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 4:42pm

Malacañang welcomed the ruling declaring former president Rodrigo Duterte fit to stand trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC), stating that Filipinos hope he remains healthy enough to face the court and answer for his administration’s drug war killings.
Duterte, who faces crimes against humanity charges, was found fit to stand trial on Thursday by the ICC Trial Chamber III.

“‘Yun naman din po ang nais natin. Unang-una, ang nais lahat ng mga Pilipino ay maging maayos ang kalusugan ng dating Pangulong Duterte — mas maging malakas siya, mas maging malalim ang kaniyang mga pag-iisip para maharap niya ang mga akusasyon na ibinabato sa kaniya,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said Friday.
(That is also what we want. First of all, all Filipinos wish former President Duterte good health—for him to be stronger and maintain mental clarity so he can face the accusations against him.)
To accommodate Duterte's participation, Trial Chamber III ordered special measures for the trial, which is set to begin on November 30, 2026.
According to Castro, it is only by maintaining good health that the former president can reveal the truth regarding his anti-drug campaign.
She noted that when it is Duterte's turn to speak, he might finally confess to the killings carried out under his “alleged drug war.”

“Dahil sa kaniyang maging malusog na pangangatawan [at] malusog na pag-iisip, doon lamang niya maaaring isiwalat ang katotohanan. At malamang ay mababanggit niya rin sa hearing kapag panahon na niyang magsalita, ang pag-amin niya sa mga isinagawang planong pagpapatay para sa paglaban di-umano sa droga,” Castro said.

(Only through good physical health and mental clarity can he reveal the truth. And when it is his turn to testify during the hearing, he will likely admit to the planned killings carried out in the name of his alleged war on drugs.)
Prior to the third status conference on September 16, Duterte’s defense team had requested that the Chamber order additional medical evaluations.

His lead counsel, Peter Haynes, previously argued that an earlier examination revealed "significant memory impairment," leaving the former president unable to retain new information or consistently recall past events.
In its decision, Trial Chamber III also instructed the ICC Registry to “make necessary arrangements” for the upcoming trial.

In its observation filed on October 7, the Registry asked the Chamber to consider its “recommended special measures,” including a sitting schedule of one-hour blocks and permitting remote attendance via video link from the ICC Detention Center. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: EXPLAINER: What are LOA, eCAR, transfer of deeds mentioned in VP Sara's impeachment trial?
articles.summary: EXPLAINER: What are LOA, eCAR, transfer of deeds mentioned in VP Sara"s impeachment trial?

blocks.text: Published October 9, 2026 4:35pm

During the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) and land registry officials have testified about the alleged unexplained wealth of the second-highest elected official in the country.
BIR representatives mentioned the issuance of a letter of authority (LOA) for the audit of the tax records of Duterte and her husband, Atty. Manases Carpio.

Likewise, during the trial, BIR representatives testified that there is no record of an Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) for the reported sale or transfer of Cale88 Foods Corporation shares.
Land registry officials testified about real properties linked to Carpio that were allegedly missing or mismatched in the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).
It was alleged that Duterte’s SALN, which she filed jointly with Carpio, did not contain the P6 million property acquired by the latter in July 2024.
Some of the terms mentioned during the trial may sound technical, especially to those who are not familiar with the tax and asset transfer process.
The terms mentioned are the following:
LOA (Letter of Authority)
The BIR defines Letter of Authority (LOA) as a primary legal document that authorizes revenue officers to examine a taxpayer's books and records.
The taxman said a LOA grants the agency the authority to conduct audits based on a clear legal foundation, with proper identification of the examiner and adherence to due process.
Complementing the LOA is the Mission Order (MO) —an administrative instrument for authorizing surveillance, verification, site inspections, and other limited fact-finding activities.
Unlike LOA, an MO does not authorize audits, examination of books of account, or the issuance of assessments.
According to the BIR, the order applies to all its operating offices that conduct field audits and related field operations, including but not limited to:

items: Large Taxpayers Service (LTS)
Revenue Regions (RRs)
Revenue District Offices (RDOs)
National and Regional Investigation Divisions
Assessment Divisions
VAT Audit Unit (LTS)
VAT Audit Sections
Office Audit Sections
All other offices, committees, and task forces authorized to conduct examinations, verification of taxpayers' books of account, records, and other related transactions or investigations.

blocks.text: eCAR (Electronic-Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR)

An eCAR serves as tax clearance proving that all applicable taxes —such as Capital Gains Tax, Donor’s Tax, or Estate Tax— have been fully paid for the transfer of real property like land or houses or personal property such as shares of stock.

The BIR said that the eCAR being issued by the taxman allows the Land Registration Authority (LRA) to transfer ownership of real properties resulting from sale, donation, and other modes of transfer. The CAR is issued by the BIR as a proof that the transfer of property was reported and that all necessary taxes were paid in full by the taxpayer.
Transfer of deeds

Meanwhile, the transfer of deeds refers to the process of settling internal revenue taxes at the BIR and securing a Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR) when transferring real property ownership in the Philippines
—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: UAAP suspends Ateneo coach Louie Alas for one game
articles.summary: Just days after losing to rival La Salle, the Ateneo Blue Eagles look to rebound against the FEU Tamaraws minus head coach Louie Alas

blocks.text: MENTOR. Ateneo coach Louie Alas (left) instructs his players on court.
UAAP
Just days after losing to rival La Salle, the Ateneo Blue Eagles look to rebound against the FEU Tamaraws minus head coach Louie Alas
MANILA, Philippines – The UAAP suspended Ateneo head coach Louie Alas on Friday, October 9, after accumulating three infractions in the men’s basketball tournament.
Alas will serve a one-game suspension on Saturday, October 10, when the Blue Eagles battle the Far Eastern University Tamaraws at the Araneta Coliseum.
Ateneo, fresh from a loss to rival La Salle, remains locked in a three-way tie for second at 3-2, behind FEU (3-1) early in the first round of Season 89.

Alas committed two of his three infractions during Ateneo’s game against the La Salle Green Archers on Wednesday, October 7, while his first technical foul came on September 19, during the Blue Eagles’ match against the UP Fighting Maroons.
League rules state that coaches will be slapped an automatic one-game suspension after accumulating three technical fouls or infractions.

During the Ateneo-La Salle game, Blue Eagles assistant coach Kerby Raymundo was observed verbally taunting La Salle player Vhoris Marasigan from the bench following a foul call at the 3:42 mark of the fourth quarter. Alas was subsequently assessed a direct technical foul for unsportsmanlike behavior, which was later changed to a bench technical foul.

Around the same time, Alas was observed engaging in physical misconduct when he forcefully attempted to pull a La Salle player to his feet before making further physical contact by nudging another player with his elbow.

The actions were not seen by game officials, but the Commissioner’s Office reviewed the incidents and assessed the physical misconduct as a disqualifying foul under the UAAP House Rules and applicable FIBA regulations.
During the Ateneo-UP game, Raymundo was assessed a technical foul for improper bench decorum, which was charged to Alas.
Ateneo can appeal the decision. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina will soon have a new Grand Mufti
articles.summary: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire…

image.caption: The headquarters of the Islamic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina are in SarajevoImage: Samir Huseinović/DW

blocks.text: The reis-ul-ulema or Grand Mufti of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the head of the country's Islamic community, represents the interests of Muslims before the state, expresses himself on political, moral and social issues and defends the independence of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina against attempts at foreign influence.
Having served two seven-year terms, the current Grand Mufti, Husein Kavazovic, is no longer permitted to run.

Three candidates are competing to become his successor: Salem Dedovic, the Mufti of Mostar, Nedzad Grabus, the Mufti of Sarajevo, and Mensur Malkic, the head of the Directorate for Religious Affairs of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Grand Mufti's envoy.

While Malkic's focus lies in strengthening the Islamic Community in religious and institutional terms, Dedovic has stated that he sees the office in a more political light and would like it to become more engaged in social debates. Grabus, who has the most international experience as the former Grand Mufti of Slovenia, says he would like to strengthen the community in times of globalization and secularization.

"No other Islamic personality in Europe holds a position like the Reis-ul-ulema in Sarajevo," said Imam Benjamin Idriz, the head of the Islamic Community in the Bavarian city of Penzberg and the chair of the Munich Forum for Islam. "That's why the importance of this election extends far beyond the country, to Muslims and non-Muslims alike, across Europe."

blocks.caption: Grand Mufti Husein Kavazovic has reached the end of his two termsImage: Samir Jordamovic/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: The President of the Islamic Community of Bosniaks in Germany (IGBD), Zenahir Mrakovic, said that the "election is important to us, because historically, theologically and institutionally, we share close ties with the Islamic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina."
"Bosniak" is the name Bosnian Muslims use for themselves. With around 100 communities across the country, the IGBD is one of Germany's smaller Muslim associations.

Muslims have lived in Bosnia and Herzegovina for centuries. Islam was introduced to the population when to Ottoman Empire spread through southeastern Europe. The organizational structure of the Islamic Communities was established after the Berlin Congress in 1878, which, among other things, placed Bosnia and Herzegovina under Austro-Hungarian rule.

Following the example of Christian churches, the Austro-Hungarian rulers soon officially recognized Islam as a religious community and in 1882, they founded the Council of Ulema and appointed the first Reis-ul-ulema as president.
Unique self-organization of the Muslim faith

This kind of Islamic self-organization could become a model for Muslims across Europe. The Islamic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina is independent from the state and is financed with donations, membership fees and zakat, a form of charity given by Muslims.

The Islamic Community has its own sort of parliament, the Sabor, and a Constitutional Court that ensures the community's actions are in line with the constitution of the country in which it operates. The Riyaset is the community's highest executive body, responsible for implementing decisions. Its headquarters are in Sarajevo.

In the 150 years since its founding, the Islamic Community of Bosnia and Herzegovina has survived numerous political upheavals and repeatedly adapted to new circumstances. After the Ottoman Empire came the Habsburg monarchy and Austro-Hungarian rule, then the Kingdom of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Yugoslavia under Josip Broz Tito. Following Tito's death, the Bosnian War for independence ended in 1995 with the Dayton Accords.

Today, Bosnia and Herzegovina is a secular state with a democratic constitutional order. Time and again, the Islamic Community has clearly distanced itself from radical tendencies. It has a history of cooperation and coexistence with Jewish and Christian communities.
This has also left an impression on the roughly 400,000 Bosnian Muslims living in Germany.

"In the process of institutionalizing Islam in Germany, the experience of the Bosniaks' Islamic Community should be taken more strongly into account," said Esnaf Begic, a former imam and a lecturer at the Institute for Islamic Theology at Osnabrück University. "We are autochthonous European Muslims and to a certain extent, we share more similarities with Germans than with Muslims from Afghanistan, Iran or Saudi Arabia."

Mrakovic, head of the IGBD, agrees that Bosnia's experience with organizing religious life in a democratic and pluralistic society could also be useful to other Muslim communities. "It's not about telling other people how to live their Islamic faith but about learning from our own experiences: how we preserve our religious identity while remaining a natural part of European, democratic society.

blocks.caption: Islamic feminism is more widespread in Bosnia and HerzegovinaImage: Samir Huseinović/DW

blocks.text: An office in challenging times

The new head of Bosnian Muslims will be assuming his role in challenging times. Statehood in Bosnia and Herzegovina remains fragile, and foreign actors are vying for more influence. "Attempts to exert more influence aren't only coming from Ankara or Riyah, but also from Washington, Berlin or Brussels. They, too are, trying to act upon the Reis-ul-ulema in their own interest," Begic said.

In Europe, anti-Muslim racism and Islamophobia have reached levels that are becoming increasingly frightening for Muslims. Right-wing populists are on the rise, and extremist parties are attracting more and more supporters bent on denying Muslims the right to participate in society.
Given the circumstances, the new Reis-ul-ulema will be expected to employ the full democratic and historical legitimacy of his office to actively engage in debates about Islam in Europe.

This is what Idriz, the imam from Penzberg, hopes for, too. He believes the new Reis-ul-ulema could inspire more confidence not only in Bosniaks, but in all European Muslims, while signaling to majority societies that Islam is a part of Europe, and that it affirms and embraces values such as the rule of law, gender equality and freedom of expression. "In the future, the Reis-ul-ulema should lay an even stronger emphasis on this," Idriz said.
This article was originally published in German.
